stages.title: Initial screen
stages.text:
# Case 01 — The smaller store network

**Historical reconstruction from public filings; not an original Value Line report.** Company names are masked. Information cutoff: May 1, 2009. Figures below cover fiscal years, not calendar years. This case is selected for learning; it is not guaranteed to be a good investment or to pass your screen.

## First-pass packet

Company A sells discretionary home decorations through leased U.S. stores. It is a retailer, not a franchisor. Its financial performance depends on merchandise selection, markdowns, customer traffic, and rent. Holiday sales are especially important.

Amounts are **$ millions**, except EPS. Parentheses indicate losses or cash outflows. Capex is shown as a positive amount spent.

| Metric | FY2006 | FY2007 | FY2008 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Net sales | 443.248 | 395.929 | 390.640 |
| GAAP net income | (0.140) | (25.906) | 9.305 |
| Diluted EPS, dollars | (0.01) | (1.33) | 0.47 |
| Cash from operations | 29.483 | (4.879) | 29.562 |
| Capital expenditure | 19.505 | 14.835 | 2.740 |
| Year-end cash | 25.358 | 5.820 | 36.445 |
| Year-end bank revolver borrowing | 0 | 0 | 0 |

FY2006 contains 53 weeks; the other years contain 52. Net sales exclude separately reported gift-card/certificate breakage revenue. Bank borrowing excludes lease commitments.

No verified price at the information cutoff is supplied. First decide whether the business deserves attention and what information you need to estimate value. A good business at an unknown price is not yet a demonstrated investment opportunity.

```text
Income statement         Cash-flow statement         Balance sheet
sales → costs → profit   profit → cash adjustments   cash / inventory
                         → CFO − capex               vs obligations
        │                         │                         │
        └──────── Is the improvement repeatable? ───────────┘
```

## Screening questions — mental math is sufficient

1. Roughly how much did sales fall in each of the last two years? What changed in profitability?
2. Calculate CFO minus capex in all three years. Which part of the latest improvement needs the most explanation?
3. Does zero year-end bank borrowing establish low financial risk? Name two missing checks.
4. Is FY2008 EPS an adequate standalone estimate of annual earning power? What would you investigate before multiplying it by a P/E?
5. Choose **investigate / pass / insufficient information**. Give at most two reasons and your single most valuable next question.

Stop here before opening the second-stage packet. You are allowed to pass. The aim is to make a reasoned decision with incomplete information, not guess the historical winner.

**Lesson:** distinguish a change in the business from a change in the number of stores included in the average.

Sources are held in a separate tutor file to preserve anonymity; they are disclosed at the reveal.

stages.title: Second-stage diligence
stages.text:
# Case 01 — Second-stage evidence

Same May 1, 2009 information cutoff. No later outcomes are included. Rounded figures from the contemporary annual filing.

| Evidence | FY2007 | FY2008 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Year-end stores | 335 | 299 |
| Comparable-store sales change | −13.3% | +3.6% |
| Gross margin | 28.7% | 34.5% |
| Inventory, $m | 41.246 | 38.686 |

Management attributes improvement partly to fewer markdowns and lower occupancy costs. In FY2008 the company opened 3 stores and closed 39. Future minimum operating-lease payments total approximately $251m; about $47m is due in FY2009. FY2008 pretax income was $10.088m and tax expense $0.783m. Cash received from selling property/equipment was $3.700m, classified in investing activities.

## Diligence questions

1. Draw two explanations for rising margins: one durable and one temporary. Which evidence would distinguish them?
2. Could closing weak stores raise reported average store performance without improving every surviving location? How does comparable-store sales information help, and what does it still leave unanswered?
3. Is $36m cash all surplus cash distributable to shareholders? Consider the calendar, inventory purchases, and leases.
4. Approximate the effective tax rate. For a sensitivity exercise—not a prediction—what would net income be at a 35% tax rate? Why might this matter to valuation?
5. Build a conservative range for annual cash earning power. Do not simply annualize the best quarter or assume this year's capex is permanent. State what evidence you still need before setting a purchase price.

## Where to look next in the historical filing

```text
Question                         Relevant section
Why margins changed              MD&A: gross profit / operating expenses
How much cash is seasonal        Liquidity + quarterly-results table
What rent must be paid           Long-term leases note
Why taxes are unusually low      Income-tax note
Whether closures are economical  Store-count table + lease/impairment notes
```

Before the reveal, write three sentences: your decision, the evidence that would reverse it, and your largest unresolved uncertainty.
